title: Amar Kale Paints Karnataka in Chilli and Turmeric for a World Record
excerpt: The Dharwad artist's 175.82-square-metre spice painting of Karnataka and the Hampi Chariot is the largest ever, made from 11 kg of two kitchen spices.
body:
• Amar Kale, 29, of Dharwad, Karnataka, set the Guinness World Record for the largest spice painting: 175.82 square metres (1,892.5 sq ft), about two-thirds the size of a tennis court.
  • He used only two kitchen spices — about 5 kg of chilli powder and 6 kg of turmeric — to draw the outline of Karnataka featuring the Hampi Chariot, completing the work in around 10 hours on 27 January.
  • It is Kale's third Guinness title, after the most painted handprints in one minute in 2021 and the largest painting by mouth, at 112.36 square metres, set in February.
  • For food lovers: the yellow and red of turmeric and chilli were chosen because they are the colours associated with Karnataka — the painting is literally made from the state's pantry.

An artist has painted Karnataka in the contents of its kitchens. Amar Kale, a 29-year-old professional artist from Dharwad, claimed the Guinness World Record for the largest spice painting with a work measuring 175.82 square metres (1,892.5 sq ft), Guinness World Records reported. The painting, created in Dharwad on 27 January, is about two-thirds the size of a tennis court.

Two spices, one state

Kale used only turmeric and chilli powder — around 5 kg of chilli and 6 kg of turmeric — mixed as his pigment. Inside the outline of Karnataka he drew the Hampi Chariot, the stone chariot that is one of the state's best-known monuments. Surplus spice he had prepared was donated so none of it went to waste, Guinness said, and the finished painting went on public display after the attempt.

"Karnataka is known for its spices, so I chose everyday kitchen spices as my artistic medium. I used only turmeric and chilli powder because their natural yellow and red tones represent the colours associated with Karnataka."

— Amar Kale, artist

"This artwork was my small contribution towards showcasing Karnataka's rich culture, heritage, art and architecture to the world," Kale said. "For me, this painting is more than a record attempt — it is an artistic tribute to Karnataka and its rich heritage." Curly Tales' account of the record shows the process: the powders mixed with water and applied with a large brush onto a white surface.

A self-taught artist on his third record

Kale is self-taught and has worked professionally for around eight years, specialising in realistic works and portraits in oils and acrylics. He first picked up a brush inspired by his father, also an artist, completed a diploma in mechanical engineering, and left an engineering job in 2018 to paint full-time.

The spice painting is his third Guinness title. He first entered the record books in 2021 with 98 painted handprints in one minute — a mark since broken with 99 — and in February set the record for the largest painting by mouth by an individual, at 112.36 square metres (1,209.43 sq ft). "Becoming a Guinness World Records title holder was once a dream; becoming a three-time title holder has been a journey of creativity, persistence and self-belief," he said.

Why it resonates beyond the record

For diaspora readers, the appeal is the medium as much as the scale. Turmeric and chilli are the two powders no Indian kitchen — in Dharwad or in New Jersey — is without. Kale's point was explicit: "I also wanted to show that extraordinary art can be created from the simplest materials. Spices that we use every day in our kitchens can also become a medium for creating a large-scale historical artwork." He hopes to attempt further art records.
